questions.q: Which context variable is NOT available in a delete trigger?
options: Trigger.old
Trigger.oldMap
Trigger.new
Trigger.isDelete
questions.explain: A record being deleted has no 'new' version, so Trigger.new does not exist in delete triggers — only Trigger.old and Trigger.oldMap are available.

questions.q: In an insert trigger, which record-list variable is unavailable?
options: Trigger.old
Trigger.new
Trigger.newMap (in an after-insert trigger)
None — all record-list variables are always available
questions.explain: A brand-new record has no prior version, so Trigger.old (and Trigger.oldMap) is not available on insert.

options: Whether the trigger fired due to an insert
The number of records in the batch
Whether the current Apex code is running inside a trigger context at all
Whether the trigger is in its before or after phase
questions.explain: Trigger.isExecuting is true whenever the running code is in a trigger context, which is useful in helper methods that might also be called from outside a trigger.

options: The total number of fields on the sObject
The number of records in the current trigger invocation (batch)
The number of trigger events listed in the trigger definition
The maximum number of records Salesforce will ever allow in one DML statement
questions.explain: Trigger.size is an Integer giving the count of records in the current batch, which can be up to 200 at a time.

questions.q: In a before update trigger, how can you compare a record's new value against its prior value for the same field?
options: Use Trigger.oldMap.get(record.Id) alongside the record from Trigger.new
Compare against Trigger.size
There is no way to see the prior value in a before update trigger
Use Trigger.isBefore to look up the old value
questions.explain: Trigger.oldMap, keyed by Id, lets you look up each record's prior version to compare against the current version found while iterating Trigger.new.
